stem:
Anaya hears that elephants have entered farms and villages after forest cover fell, vegetation became scarce, rainfall patterns changed, and waterholes dried in the natural habitat.

Which claims correctly explain why the animals moved? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: When vegetation becomes scarce in the natural habitat, elephants may move into farms in search of food.
When waterholes dry in the natural habitat, elephants may move near villages in search of water.
Elephants prefer villages for company even when forest food and water are plentiful.
Rainfall, forest cover, and waterholes have no link to where elephants find food and water.

teacher.key_rationale: Scarce vegetation and dried waterholes push animals to seek food and water in farms and villages. Preferring villages when habitat is plentiful, or denying links to rainfall and cover, miss that hinge.
